newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to fulfill Maastricht criteria - Stark.
newsitem.headline: Germany to fulfill Maastricht criteria - Stark.

text.p: Germany will fulfill the criteria this year required to qualify for European monetary union despite revising up its budget deficit forecast, Finance State Secretary Juergen Stark said on Tuesday.

"I believe and I am convinced that we will meet the Maastricht criteria in 1997. We are open and honest," Stark, who is number two to Finance Minister Theo Waigel, told a conference of German newspaper editors.

Stark said economic developments in Germany, particularly rising unemployment, were to blame for raising the country's budget deficit forecast to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product. Waigel's 1997 budget foresaw a 2.5-percent deficit.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Tuesday approved an annual government economic report that contained the new deficit forecast.
The report confirmed a growth forecast of 2.5 percent but said the unemployment rate would rise to a higher-than-expected 11 percent this year from 10.3 percent last year.
The Maastricht reaty specifies a three-percent ceiling for new government borrowing for countries to qualify for the launch of the single European currency, planned in 1999.
